lesson_title: The Queue That Doesn't Move: Understanding Unemployment
hook_text: Same town. One queue is 300 people. The other is 3. That's the whole story.
clip_script: Six in the morning at a factory gate. The queue is long, quiet, mostly young — matric certificates in plastic sleeves, CVs printed at the internet café. The gate opens. Two people go in. The rest come back tomorrow. Now walk down the road to the engineering firm. Their queue is three people long — and they're phoning agencies because they can't fill the post. Same town. Opposite problem. That's the thing most conversations about unemployment miss: it isn't ONE thing. The graduate waiting between school and a February start — that's a gap, and it closes. The retrenched mineworker whose shaft shut and whose skills fit nothing nearby — that's a MISMATCH, and no better job advert will touch it. The worker retrenched because orders dried up countrywide — that lifts when the economy lifts. Five different stories, five different fixes. And the people who stopped coming to the queue entirely — because they stopped believing the gate opens? The official count doesn't see them at all.
visual_style: Pre-dawn gate with a long silent queue, breath visible; cut to a short queue at a glass-fronted firm with a ringing phone; the two queues rendered side by side as bar heights; figures quietly stepping out of the long queue and greying out.
mood: Sober, respectful, clear-eyed — dignity first, analysis second.
pacing: Slow observational open, sharpening at the contrast, brisk through the five stories, quiet landing.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and learn to diagnose before prescribing.
